about: Every point value the screener uses. Read by osv_sourcer.py (prescore, compute_signals, score_entry); nothing in the code hard-codes a point any more. After editing, re-score the index offline with: python3 sourcer/osv_sourcer.py classify. v1 (a 0-10 reader rubric no code ever read) is kept in weights.v1.json; v2 (literature-only) in weights.v2.json.
evidence: ../research/owasp_top10_findings.md (CWE-bench v1 per-category and per-CWE data, official OWASP Top 10:2025 mapping, ~15 vulnerability-repair studies). Key result: the fix's SHAPE (files, hunks, lines, sites) predicts repair failure far better than its CWE or OWASP category, so fix-shape signals carry the most points and the weakness signal is deliberately modest.

multi_site._note: S1. The SAME trust decision enforced at several independent sites (measured: the same new check added at N sites in the upstream fix). Its value is INJECTABILITY: siblings can only be planted where the decision recurs; a single choke point cannot host siblings (async-sib, tomcat-sib were abandoned for this). It also adds difficulty (CWE-bench: closing 2 of 3 sites scores zero). NOT the same as symptom-fix distance (S2) or fix size (S6).

cause_other_layer._note: S2. Symptom-fix DISPARITY: the bug shows in one place (endpoint, crash site, reported function) but the fix belongs in another function, file or layer. This is LOCALISATION, the dominant repair failure in every source (PatchBench: 64% of agent patches stay on the crash trace when the real fix is elsewhere; VulnRepairEval: 60-78% of failures; CWE-bench: 'fix where tokens are created, not where they are cancelled'). Currently detected only from advisory wording (weak, rare); a computed version is proposed in research/owasp_top10_findings.md.

symptom_fix_disparity._note: S2 computed parts (added 2026-10-16), shown in score_detail as labels. S2a named-location disparity (research/owasp_top10_findings.md section 7): locations the advisory names (functions, classes, files, endpoints, CLI commands; adv_signals.named) vs the files and enclosing definitions the fix changes (commit shape: changed_files, hunk_funcs, units). States: disparity = names locations, fix touches none (lenient touch, so conservative); on_named = every changed site is in a named function/class/file; partial = some of each; unknown = nothing named. S2b data producer off the check's path (Hadi 2026-10-15; ALGORITHM.md 'Trap calibration'): the fix changes a check-role site (auth, permission, policy, guard, middleware, validate/verify/check, access, acl, token) AND a producer-role site (schema, serializer, parser, loader, decoder, unmarshal, codec, model, types, constructor/new/from_*, migration, store) in a DIFFERENT file; role from the enclosing definition's name, else the file name, else the nearest directories. 'check_does_not_call_producer' needs the vulnerable tree (siblings stage, not built): commit shape s2b.check_calls_producer stays null until then.
symptom_fix_disparity._validation: research/round1-analysis/D-computed-s2.md (2026-10-16). All points 0 until validated on more outcomes.
symptom_fix_disparity._credit: S2b: Hadi 2026-10-15 (DeepSeek missed the producer 8/8; MCP TypeScript SDK GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h).

defence_ineffective._note: S3. A defence existed and did not work.

bypass_and_siblings._note: S4. Earlier fix incomplete, or several advisories in the same package and CWE within 120 days.

weakness._note: S5. Category points come from the best CWE that maps to OWASP Top 10:2025 (directly, or through its nearest mapped ancestor in MITRE's Research view CWE-1000); 'unmapped' only when no CWE maps. The per-CWE adjustment is the highest over all the advisory's CWEs (exact CWE only; not inherited from parents). Plus the abstract-only and LLM bonuses. Deliberately modest: CWE labels predict repair difficulty weakly (localisation is the strongest, most consistent predictor).

category_points._source: CWE-bench v1/v0: only the extremes are stable across versions (A08, A06 hardest; A01, A04 easiest for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash).

cwe_adjustments._precedence: disputed first (always 0), then the highest-points list that contains the CWE

disputed._source: easy or saturated in CWE-bench/BaxBench but hard on real CVEs (VulnRepairEval, LiveCVEBench, CWEFT) or strongly language-dependent
disputed._v3: 287 moved here from saturated: 2 of 3 CWE-287 bases produced real model defects (async-http-client both models, rclone DeepSeek).

hard_across_sources._source: hard in >= 2 independent repair sources (CWE-bench, CodeRover-S, PatchAgent, SAN2PATCH, CWEFT, Garg et al., VulnRepairEval)

hard_in_cwe_bench._source: CWE-bench v1: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash <= 25% and 11-model mean <= 50% (research/cwe_bench_v1_cwe.tsv); mostly 1-2 tasks each

deepseek_weak_spot._source: CWE-bench v1: DeepSeek <= 25% while the 11-model mean is > 50%
deepseek_weak_spot._v3: 347 removed: DeepSeek solved both CWE-347 tasks (hickory-dns 25 min, ruby-saml 16 min).

easy_to_repair._source: easy in >= 2 repair sources (LiveCVEBench, BaxBench, CWE-bench)

saturated._source: CWE-bench v1: mean >= 90% and DeepSeek 100%, not contradicted elsewhere

abstract_only._source: CWEFT (ESEM 2026) and the Vul4J study: broad classes are repaired 0-3% (CWE-20 3.1%, 284/264/269 0%). Applies when EVERY CWE on the advisory is in this list, is Pillar level, or is not a weakness entry at all (a category such as 264 or 16). NOT all MITRE 'Class' CWEs: that fired on 31% of candidates, mostly 862/863/287, which are everyday labels, not vague ones (it would have re-rewarded A01). CWE-bench v1 context: DeepSeek 47% on Class-level CWEs vs 59% on Base.

weakness._favoured_note: c_favoured_class = 1 when the weakness points reach this; it gates Python/JS proposals and excludes a candidate from the easy controls.

llm_in_the_loop._source: LiL paper (arXiv 2605.28893): bugs where an app executes or renders LLM OUTPUT are fixed ~26% on average, 15.5 points below conventional bugs; DeepSeek-V4-Pro 0/4 on output rendering. Detected from the advisory summary only, by wording that says model output drives the action.

llm_ecosystem._source: Same paper: ordinary bugs in LLM apps/frameworks (IDOR, SSRF, auth in Open WebUI, Flowise, MCP servers, vLLM...) are only ~5 points harder than conventional bugs (36.6% vs 41.3% fixed). Label only (0 points) until our own runs say otherwise; not added when the bug is already LLM-in-the-loop.

top25_label._source: Decision 2026-10-16 (option c, label only): CWE-bench v1 shows Top 25 CWEs are EASIER for models (DeepSeek 67% vs 52%, 24 vs 96 tasks), which conflicts with their realism value to the client. Recorded per candidate for later analysis; changes no score. Revisit with our own trial results (options were -1 difficulty / +1 realism).

attack_label._source: Decision 2026-10-16 (option a, label only): item 5 (research/attack_taxonomies_findings.md). Across 13 repair benchmarks, CVEs whose CWE maps (CWE->CAPEC->ATT&CK, ancestor fallback) to ATT&CK credential-access or CAPEC 'Collect and Analyze Information' are fixed 8-19 pts less often, also within OWASP category, within our screener points and for DeepSeek runs; but null in LiveCVEBench (the agentic benchmark closest to ours) and the chain is noisy. Recorded per candidate; changes no score. Revisit with our own trial results (option b was +1).

fix_shape._note: S6. The strongest predictor found (PatchEval: 20% repaired at 1 file, 0% at 3+; 25% at 1 hunk, ~0% at 3+; 33% at 1-5 lines, 2% at 50+).
fix_shape._cap_note: Not because S1 and S6 mean the same (S1 = one decision repeated, i.e. injectability; S6 = fix size/spread), but because the SAME hunks feed both: a check added at 3 sites is also a 3-hunk fix. The cap stops that one piece of evidence from counting twice.
fix_shape._v3: Halved: fix size did not predict failure inside our band (rho -0.3..+0.1); it tracked only time and tool calls. single_compact_hunk -3 kept (PatchEval's 1-vs-3+ file effect is untested by us).

overbroad_repair._note: S7, reader judgement only. v3: also yes when a nearby LEGITIMATE behaviour must keep working (a linked/permitted value next to the hidden one, protocol-relative URLs, a normal-size input next to a size cap). Over-broad/regression defects: 8 jackson-family runs (both models), webob MiMo.

undisclosed_siblings._note: S8 (v3, strongest own evidence). The same trust decision recurs at sites the advisory and the upstream fix do NOT name: other call sites of the guard or sink at the vulnerable commit, a handler of the same family with no check at all, or an alternate route to the same sink (defaults/merged config). jackson-databind-sib (sibling not named): DeepSeek 0/6; jackson-sib7 (named): 8/11; rclone-sib/russh-sib (all named): solved. Judged by a reader; computed by `osv_sourcer.py siblings` (search of the vulnerable tree).

trap_labels._note: Labels (0 points) recorded per candidate by a reader; each was one real model defect in round 1. Score once a label has >= 3 cases.

adjacent_adjustment_logic.example: asyncssh: guard placed after the dropbear -= 1 adjustment

fail_open_fallback.example: rclone: fell back to the access key id when the proxy returned no secret

parser_mismatch.example: async-http-client: strict cookie decoder dropped the caller's value

linked_visible_value.example: jackson: a permitted property linked to the hidden one; over-broad fixes broke it

upstream_fix_public.example: not a difficulty signal offline; lookup runs solved 38/38 with internet

prescore._note: Order of the diff-fetch queue, from advisory-only signals (the diff is not known yet). Weakness points are added as computed for S5.

owasp_map._note: Official OWASP Top 10:2025 lists (249 CWEs), plus the entries below: OWASP's A03 typo (lists 447, means 477) and the 9 CWEs CWE-bench places although OWASP does not map them. With ancestor_fallback, a CWE not in any list takes the category of its nearest ancestor that is (MITRE CWE 4.20 Research view): 97 of 173 previously unmapped candidates gain a category this way.

evidence_v3: Round-1 own results (research/round1-analysis/A-screener-validity.md, B-failure-modes.md): v2 ranked our 6 mined bases at rho -0.06 vs difficulty (v1 +0.66). v3 changes are fitted in-sample on those 6 bases (rho +0.76) and are a HYPOTHESIS to re-check in round 2. Difficulty came from undisclosed siblings / alternate paths (S8), not from fix size or advisory wording.
